clue.text: Sycophant once left sitting in an agony of suspense

definitions.meaning: a flattering courtier of ancient Syracuse at the court of Dionysius

definitions.text: left sitting in an agony of suspense
definitions.meaning: the same figure was seated at a feast beneath a sword hung by a single hair

explanation.surface: A fawning hanger-on of old is kept waiting, squirming with anxiety.
explanation.definitionFit: The legend of the courtier seated beneath a hanging sword gives the name of the man who fawned on Dionysius and then sat in terror.

clue.text: Only half of William's book is in the vault

indicators.note: only half of says to keep the first half of the book's name

parts.note: the Domesday Book was the great survey of England ordered by William the Conqueror

explanation.surface: Just half of a book by William can be found in the cellar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vault' looks like a strongroom where a book is kept, but it is the arched roof.
explanation.definitionFit: A dome is a rounded vault forming a roof.

clue.text: All join the Green party?

parts.note: everyone signing up to one political party would be a way of uniting in a shared aim; in the surface it suggests mass membership of the environmentalists

explanation.surface: Imagine everyone signing up to the environmentalist party.
explanation.definitionFit: To make common cause is to unite with others in pursuit of a shared goal, as everyone joining one party would.

clue.text: Herb is my co-star in play

indicators.note: in play suggests the letters are moved about freely

explanation.surface: An actor introduces Herb as the partner in a theatre production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Herb' reads as a man's name, but it is the definition: a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Costmary is an aromatic herb related to tansy, once used to flavour ale.

clue.text: Girl wants correct husband

parts.note: to edit a text is to correct it

explanation.surface: A young woman wants to fix her husband.
explanation.definitionFit: Edith is a common English female given name, so it serves as an example of a girl.

clue.text: Party meeting soundly shut us up

indicators.note: the clue word asks us to say the phrase out loud and write what we hear

parts.note: to caulk is to seal up a gap, so 'shut us up' gives caulk us

explanation.surface: At a political gathering, someone firmly silences the speakers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soundly' looks like 'firmly' in the surface, but it signals a homophone: caulk us, spoken, gives the word for a party meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A closed meeting of members of a political party to choose candidates or policy is a well-known synonym.

clue.text: One admits copper's charge

indicators.note: admits means the one word lets the copper's letters in

parts.note: an ace is the one in a pack of cards
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper; the 's adds an S

explanation.surface: A suspect admits a charge brought by the police officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a police officer, but it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: To accuse someone is to charge them with an offence.

clue.text: Range over island with only one pound in box? For pity's sake!

indicators.note: in a down answer, over places the range word above the island

parts.note: compass means range or scope

indicators.note: with only one says that of the two letters for pound just one is kept

parts.note: 'the box' is British slang for television, so being in it is being on a telly
L, from Latin libra, is the abbreviation for pound

explanation.surface: Someone frets that a TV show got only a pound, begging for mercy.
explanation.walkthrough: ON A TELLY loses one of its two Ls to give ONATELY. 'box' is the British slang for a television set.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something compassionately means acting out of pity, so 'for pity's sake' describes it loosely.

clue.text: Single woman gets excited about plain ring

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go around the other pieces
excited suggests agitation, so the letters of gets are stirred up

parts.note: one means single
hen is slang for a woman, as in hen party

explanation.surface: An unmarried woman gets worked up over a wedding ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' scrambles GETS into ST...GE, which wraps the other pieces. 'plain' looks like an adjective but is Salisbury Plain in Wiltshire, where the famous stone ring stands.
explanation.definitionFit: Stonehenge is the prehistoric stone circle standing on Salisbury Plain in southern England.

clue.text: A colleague's not to be locked up without key

indicators.note: to be locked means held between the other pieces

parts.note: an ally is a partner or colleague

indicators.note: in a down answer, up says the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the word not as written, before turning

explanation.surface: A co-worker's no longer to be imprisoned without the key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the word NOT, giving TON; 'colleague' with 's stands for 'colleague is' in the surface but just gives the ally.
explanation.definitionFit: Atonal music has no key, so music played atonally is played without key.

clue.text: Substitute order for couturier?

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective or noun: a temporary stand-in
a dressmaker might be told to make a shift, a simple loose dress

explanation.surface: Someone sends an alternative instruction to a fashion designer.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the word in two: a shift is a straight dress, so 'make shift' is an instruction a couturier (fashion designer) might receive.
explanation.definitionFit: Something makeshift serves as a temporary replacement for the proper thing, so it is a substitute.

clue.text: Arrange nothing for jazz band

parts.note: to comb hair is to arrange it
O, the figure zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: Someone is told to arrange nothing for a jazz group.
explanation.definitionFit: A combo is a small band of musicians, typically playing jazz or dance music.

clue.text: Lovable rogue's cut into fraud

indicators.note: cut means the last letter of the word for the rogue is cut off

parts.note: a scamp is a mischievous but likeable rascal; the 's is a link meaning 'is'

explanation.surface: A charming rascal gets a share of a swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut into' reads as 'given a share of', but 'cut' trims the final P, and 'into' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A scam is a dishonest scheme to cheat people, which is a fraud.

clue.text: Shock worker's first greeting

indicators.note: first places the worker's word before the shock word

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand
a shock can shake someone up

explanation.surface: A labourer's initial welcome comes as a surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shock worker' looks like one phrase (a hero of Soviet labour), but the two words are separate pieces, put together in reverse order.
explanation.definitionFit: Clasping and shaking hands is a common form of greeting when people meet.

clue.text: Lawyer's dull speech tricked court

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay

parts.note: prose is plain, unpoetic and so dull speech

indicators.note: tricked suggests the letters of court are fooled into a new order

explanation.surface: A barrister's tedious address misled the judges.
explanation.definitionFit: A prosecutor is the lawyer who conducts the case against a defendant in court.

clue.text: A wrongly-graded exam paper may be unusual

definitions.text: A wrongly-graded exam paper may be unusual

parts.words: A wrongly-graded exam paper may be unusual
parts.note: a paper with a wrong grade can be marked again, so it is able to be re-marked; read as one word it means extraordinary

explanation.surface: It would be rare for an exam paper to be given the wrong grade.
explanation.definitionFit: Read whole, the word means extraordinary or unusual; split, it means fit to be marked again.

clue.text: Nothing left? Fair enough

definitions.meaning: if everything is on the right side, there is nothing on the left
an expression of acceptance or agreement

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether anything remains and gets a grudging yes.
explanation.definitionFit: All right is said to agree or accept, the same as fair enough; whimsically, all on the right leaves nothing on the left.

clue.text: Piece of land lies abandoned

indicators.note: abandoned means wild or unrestrained, so the letters of lies run loose

explanation.surface: A plot of ground lies deserted.
explanation.definitionFit: An isle is an island, a piece of land surrounded by water.

clue.text: Innocent victims go down, on appearance in hearing

indicators.note: in hearing asks for the phrase to be spoken and written as heard

parts.note: to go down is to fall, and an appearance is a guise; 'on' just joins them

explanation.surface: Blameless people are brought low as soon as they show up in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hearing' looks like a court hearing, but it signals a homophone: fall guise sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Fall guys are people made to take the blame for others, innocent scapegoats.

clue.text: Downfall of white author

definitions.meaning: a fall of something from the sky, here a fall of snowflakes
C. P. ..., English novelist, whose name is also something white

explanation.surface: A writer's ruin is described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Downfall' reads as ruin but here is literal: something that falls down. The author is C. P. Snow, writer of the Strangers and Brothers novels.
explanation.definitionFit: Snow is precipitation that falls from the sky, and Snow was also the surname of a well-known British novelist.

clue.text: Gripped by drama, grand literary gathering is supportive

indicators.note: gripped by says the gathering word is held between the other two pieces

parts.note: a play is a drama
G is an abbreviation for grand, a thousand pounds or dollars
a salon is a fashionable gathering of writers and artists

explanation.surface: Caught up in the theatre, a fine book circle offers encouragement.
explanation.definitionFit: To play along is to go along with or cooperate with someone, being supportive of them.

clue.text: Robust feature of football equipment

definitions.meaning: a forceful challenge to win the ball from an opponent

explanation.surface: A sturdy item of footballing kit is described.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one phrase about kit; the split is after 'football'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tackle is a firm challenge in football, and also the gear used for a sport such as angling.

clue.text: Parrot is in care of Catherine in class

parts.note: c/o is the usual abbreviation for care of on an envelope

indicators.note: in tells us the girl's name sits inside the class abbreviation

parts.note: CL is an abbreviation for class
Katie is a pet form of Catherine

explanation.surface: A pet bird is being looked after by Catherine at school.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockatiel is a small crested Australian parrot often kept as a pet.

clue.text: Dignified movement of titular governor

indicators.note: of says the answer is taken out of the following words

explanation.surface: A stately progress by a governor in name only.
explanation.definitionFit: Largo is a musical direction for a slow and stately tempo, and a movement played in it.

clue.text: Weight old boy carries

indicators.note: carries means the boy word holds the other letter inside it

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A former pupil bears a burden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old boy' looks like one unit (a former pupil) but splits into O and LAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A load is something carried, a weight or burden.

clue.text: Girl making regular selections from Virgil's work

indicators.note: making regular selections from means every third letter, starting with the first, is dropped from the epic's title

parts.note: the Aeneid is Virgil's epic poem about Aeneas

explanation.surface: A young woman is choosing passages from the Roman poet's epic.
explanation.walkthrough: From AENEID drop the first and fourth letters (A and E), keeping the regular pattern of two letters in every three.
explanation.definitionFit: Enid is an English female given name, so it serves as an example of a girl.

clue.text: Without son, refused to work vehicle

indicators.note: without says the letter for son is removed

parts.note: workers who struck went on strike, refusing to work
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Lacking a son to help, someone would not drive the van.
explanation.definitionFit: A truck is a large road vehicle for carrying goods.

clue.text: So enormous a task for Poirot?

definitions.meaning: of a task, requiring huge strength or effort
Agatha Christie's detective is Hercule Poirot, so a job for him might be named after his first name

explanation.surface: A case so huge only the great detective could tackle it.
explanation.walkthrough: The mythical hero's labours give the adjective; Christie's detective shares his name, and Christie even wrote 'The Labours of Hercules' for him.
explanation.definitionFit: Herculean describes a task so vast that it would need the strength of the mythical hero Hercules.

clue.text: Did some humming, inflicted on our ears

indicators.note: on our ears says we hear the word rather than read it

parts.note: to wreak damage is to inflict it

explanation.surface: Someone hummed a tune and made us suffer listening to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'humming' suggests a tune, but in British slang to hum is to smell bad.
explanation.definitionFit: Humming is British slang for smelling unpleasantly, so doing some humming means stinking, which is to have reeked.

clue.text: Ordered you to be arrested as not looking straight

indicators.note: arrested means held, so the you word is held inside the ordered word

parts.note: to boss someone about is to order them
ye is an old form of you

explanation.surface: Someone was told they would be detained for a shifty glance.
explanation.definitionFit: Boss-eyed is British slang for cross-eyed or squinting, so not looking straight.
